finding: Aeolid nudibranch kleptocnidae as cross-substrate cascade-match candidate per [[user_stance_cross_substrate_cascade_matching_as_research_method]]. End-goal: theft-and-repurpose of foreign biological defensive machinery (cnidarian nematocysts). Substrate-pair: cnidarian (nematocyst source) ↔ aeolid nudibranch (cnidosac storage). Both substrates achieve self-defense via operations invisible to each other's native substrate. Six PMC-extracted anchor papers; six classes L+M+D+C+K+E + I attestable from canon.

finding: MECHANISM-PIPELINE-ATTESTED. Six-step pipeline from cnidarian prey to nudibranch defense deployment: (1) ingestion without triggering via chitin cuticle + mucus inhibition + epithelial spindles; (2) branched digestive-gland routing to cerata diverticula; (3) cnidophage engulfment with intact membrane storage; (4) post-sequestration maturation via proton transport (immature → discharge-ready); (5) cnidosac musculature contraction on predator threat; (6) cnidopore opens + cnidophage ruptures + nematocyst discharges. All steps PMC-attested.
anchor_class: L (chitin/mucus barrier topology) + D (diverticulum routing) + C (proliferation→cnidophage→cnidopore cascade) + K (proton-transport maturation threshold) + M (cnidophage membrane self/non-self discipline)
anchor_citation: Greenwood 2009 Toxicon 54:1065 PMC2783962 (mechanism review); Goodheart et al. 2018 Front Zool 15:43 PMC6234619 (three-zone cnidosac + maturation); Ekimova et al. 2022 Front Zool 19:29 PMC9670572 (proliferation/cnidophage/cnidopore zones)

finding: CLASS-M-FOREIGN-ORGANELLE-BIND-LOAD-BEARING. Cnidophage membrane discipline IS the kleptocnidae-enabling primitive. Foreign cnidocyte handled distinct from self-tissue. Membrane-encased storage means: nematocyst stays unfired during transit + maturation, fires only on membrane rupture (predator bite). Functional analog of immune-system self/non-self discrimination. Goodheart et al. 2018: 'cnidophages...incorporate kleptocnides into vacuoles'; Wikipedia/Kleptocnidy synthesis: 'cells engulf cnidocytes without triggering them.'
anchor_citation: Goodheart et al. 2018 Front Zool 15:43 PMC6234619; Greenwood 2009 Toxicon 54:1065 PMC2783962

finding: CLASS-E-CATALOG-SELECTIVITY-EMPIRICAL. Dror et al. 2025 documented complete selectivity in Caloria militaris over 258 days: zero nematocysts from scyphozoan polyps (4 species); incorporated from hydrozoan Pennaria disticha within 3-6 days. Within sequestered subset, proportions differed significantly from prey distribution (PERMANOVA R²=0.56, p<0.0001). Desmonemes over-represented (35.9%); large mastigophores under-represented (1.5%). This is Class E catalog sorted-key lookup in full force.

finding: CLASS-K-MATURATION-THRESHOLD. Immature nematocysts (Spurilla; Frick 1984 cite-by-ref) mature within cnidosac via proton transport. Asymptotic-DOF accumulation: proton gradient builds until matrix-polymerized discharge-ready state achieved. Per Goodheart et al. 2018: 'Nematocysts are not functional when taken up by the cnidophages but mature via proton transport within the cnidosac.' Same Class K signature as gravitational-time-dilation substrate-mode-population (Spike #27.5) + dark-sector last-5% (Spike #27).

finding: DIFFERENTIATOR-vs-DORID-NUDIBRANCHS. Dorids (e.g. Dendrodoris limbata) elaborate polygodial sesquiterpenoid de novo from mevalonic acid (Cimino et al. 1983 Science 219:1237 PubMed 17771309). Storage in mantle epidermis, no cerata, no diverticulum-routing cascade. Class chain F (template/biosynthesis recipe) ∘ A (content-addressed by enzyme cascade) — replaces M ∘ D ∘ C ∘ K. Loss of Class M (foreign-organelle bind) in dorids; substituted Class F (template). Aeolid vs dorid differentiator IS the M-class presence.
anchor_class: Aeolid: M ∘ D ∘ C ∘ K; Dorid: F ∘ A (biosynthesis); differentiator = Class M presence/absence
anchor_citation: Cimino et al. 1983 Science 219:1237 PubMed 17771309 (de novo polygodial); Goodheart et al. 2018 PMC6234619 (cerata/cnidosac morphology)

finding: DIFFERENTIATOR-vs-SACOGLOSSAN-KLEPTOPLASTY. Sacoglossans (Elysia chlorotica etc.) phagocytize macroalgal chloroplasts via digestive-tubule cells; long-term retention up to 10 months (Cruz & Cartaxana 2022). Same M ∘ D ∘ C prefix (foreign-organelle bind + diverticulum dispatch + cascade-orientation) but terminal Class K (discrete-threshold defense) substituted with Class L (continuous-eigenoperation photosymbiosis). Aeolid vs sacoglossan differentiator IS the terminal K vs L sub-operation. Within Cladobranchia, Phyllodesmium has converted its own cascade from K (cnidosac) to L (zooxanthellae retention) — same substitution within one clade.
anchor_class: Sacoglossan: M ∘ D ∘ C ∘ L (continuous metabolic); Aeolid: M ∘ D ∘ C ∘ K (discrete defense); differentiator = K vs L terminal
anchor_citation: Cruz & Cartaxana 2022 PLoS Biol 20:e3001857 PMC9642861; Ekimova et al. 2022 PMC9670572 (Phyllodesmium loss of kleptocnidae)

finding: DIFFERENTIATOR-vs-LOST-KLEPTOCNIDAE. Within Cladobranchia, kleptocnidae has been LOST at least 4 times: Phyllodesmium, Fionidae (Phestilla + Calma + Fiona within family), Favorinus, Bulbaeolidia (Goodheart et al. 2018; Ekimova et al. 2022). M ∘ D ∘ C anatomical prefix retained (cerata + diverticula intact) but Class K terminal (cnidosac discharge apparatus) degenerated. Independent gain-and-loss attests cleanly to cascade structure: K terminal is independently gain/loss-able while M ∘ D ∘ C prefix is conserved.
anchor_class: K (terminal) is independently mutable while M ∘ D ∘ C (prefix) is conserved within Cladobranchia
anchor_citation: Goodheart et al. 2018 Front Zool 15:43 PMC6234619; Ekimova et al. 2022 Front Zool 19:29 PMC9670572

finding: TWICE-STOLEN-NEMATOCYSTS-CASCADE-RECURSION. Krupitskaya, Ekimova & Malakhov 2025 documented Coryphella trophina eating other nudibranchs and incorporating their already-stolen nematocysts: 'stinging capsules...have been stolen twice: first by mollusks feeding on cnidarians and then by C. trophina eating the mollusks.' Cascade-composition recursion — same M ∘ D ∘ C ∘ K chain operates on its own previous output regardless of source. Confirms cascade operates on byte-shape of nematocysts, not source-context. Same composability property as cascade-on-circles per [[user_stance_cascade_lives_on_circles]].

finding: CONVERGENT-CTENOPHORE-KLEPTOCNIDAE. Ctenophore genus Haeckelia sequesters cnidarian nematocysts and arrays them on tentacles. Different phylum (Ctenophora vs Mollusca), same end-state. Tentacular canal replaces ceras diverticulum; tentacle surface replaces cnidosac; M ∘ D ∘ C ∘ K cascade structurally identical. Direct evidence that this cascade is minimum sufficient operation set for nematocyst-theft-and-repurpose — convergent evolution selects same algebraic shape. Plus flatworm kleptocnidae 6-13× independent origins (Catenulida, Macrostomorpha, Proseriata, Prolecithophora, Polycladida, Rhabdocoela) — low effective edit distance from generic predatory body plan.
anchor_class: M ∘ D ∘ C ∘ K is convergently selected across Mollusca + Ctenophora + Platyhelminthes + Acoelomorpha

finding: FERMATA-MONARCH-CARDENOLIDE-CASCADE. Monarch Danaus plexippus ingests milkweed cardenolides; resistance via Na+/K+-ATPase target-site mutations (Petschenka et al. 2013 Evolution 67:2753 cite-by-ref Wiley). Sequestered cardenolides become predator defense. Selectivity: 40% leaf cardenolide (voruscharin) NOT kept, metabolized instead — Class E selectivity present. Cascade M ∘ D ∘ E ∘ K (molecular sequestration; storage in hemolymph + cuticle rather than discrete organelle). Differentiator from kleptocnidae: substrate is molecular (no Class C cascade-orientation); Class L distribution (vascular) replaces Class C (anatomical). Future spike #133 candidate.
anchor_class: M ∘ D ∘ E ∘ K (with Class L substituting Class C for distribution substrate)
anchor_citation: Agrawal et al. 2021 PNAS 118:e2024463118 PMC8072370; Petschenka et al. 2013 Evolution 67:2753 (cite-by-ref Wiley)

finding: FERMATA-POISON-FROG-ALKALOID-CASCADE. Dendrobatid frogs sequester 900+ alkaloids from arthropod diet (ants, mites, centipedes). Uptake within 4 days. Storage in dorsal granular skin glands. Cascade M ∘ D ∘ E ∘ K with Class L distribution (vascular → skin glands). Storage is organ-level discrete (granular glands) vs cell-level discrete (cnidophages); discreteness scale differs but Class K threshold-deployment same. Future spike #134 candidate.
anchor_class: M ∘ D ∘ E ∘ K (with Class L distribution, organ-level Class K granularity)
anchor_citation: Daly et al. 1994 foundational poison-frog alkaloid sequestration (cite-by-ref); recent rapid-uptake work PMC7888741

finding: DIFFERENTIATOR-CASCADE-IDENTIFIED. The explicit cascade distinguishing kleptocnidate aeolids from all other sea slugs is: aeolids retain BOTH Class M (foreign-organelle bind) AND Class K (threshold-deployment) AND Class C (anatomical cascade-orientation through diverticulum-to-cnidosac). Dorids have lost M (substituted F biosynthesis). Sacoglossans substituted K with L (continuous photosymbiosis). Phyllodesmium/Fionidae/Favorinus/Bulbaeolidia degenerated K terminal while keeping M ∘ D ∘ C anatomy. ANSWER TO USER'S 'what cascade makes it different from other seaslugs': **Class M ∘ Class K composition** (foreign-organelle handling followed by threshold-deployment) is the kleptocnidate-aeolid signature.
anchor_class: Aeolid kleptocnidae = M ∘ D ∘ C ∘ K (full); other sea slugs lost or substituted ≥1 of {M, C, K}
anchor_citation: Composite from Goodheart et al. 2018 PMC6234619; Ekimova et al. 2022 PMC9670572; Cimino et al. 1983 PubMed 17771309; Cruz & Cartaxana 2022 PMC9642861
